newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: A weak U.S. bond market continued to dominate French bonds on Thursday, sending the March bond future down to its lowest closing level since November 25.

Analysts said nervousness in the U.S., which first knocked the market lower on December 31, was the predominant theme although a lacklustre French bond auction had weighed on prices earlier in the day.

"Right now the United States is leading the dance although I'm still among the people who believes in a (U.S.) slowdown and soft landing," Valerie Plagnol, market economist at Credit Commercial de France, said.
The French bond future first ventured into negative territory when primary dealers sold futures ahead of an OAT auction at 1000 GMT, traders said.

The Treasury managed to sell 20.86 billion francs of OATs, made up of the new 5.5 percent 2007 OAT and the TEC 10 variable rate OAT, although at 1.6, the overall bid to cover ratio was lower than in recent auctions.

Bonds were lifted briefly above Tuesday's closing level after U.S. weekly jobless claims came in higher than feared but the gloom returned when a U.S. purchasing managers report showed an acceleration in manufacturing activity.
The bond future settled at 127.92, down 0.40 on the day, and techncial analysts at Credit Agricole said 127.74 would be the next target on the way down followed by 127.54.
French bonds suffered slightly in the morning ahead of the OAT auction, but the spread between 10-year French and German bond yields then returned to minus five.
As expected the Bank of France left its intervention rate unchanged at 3.15 percent at Thursday's money market tender.
Of more interest for Bank of France watchers will be the decision, expected on Friday, about the new members of the central bank's monetary policy council.
The decision is being closely watched by financial markets for any sign of a softening in the Bank's traditionally cautious approach to monetary easing.

The mandates of two members of the council expires next week and they are believed to be part of a six to three majority backing the existing policy of maintaining French interest rates slightly above those in Germany to protect the stability of the franc against the mark.
Two others members have argued publicly that France should cut rates without waiting for German easing and a third member is believed to share that view.
The concern was that the appointment of two more dovish members could shift the balance of opinion away from supporters of the central bank's so-called franc fort policy.
The franc was relatively stable on Thursday. It slipped to a low of 3.3734 against the mark during the session but returned to 3.3702, little changed from 3.3700 on Tuesday.
March PIBOR settled down one basis point and call money returned to 3-3/16 5/16 percent after rising briefly on New Year's eve for technical reasons.
